literal: Duke Sheng of Guangping; Duke Yongle of Yangzhou; younger brother Changbi; Prince Xianguo of Xiangle; Prince Sigu of Shangluo; son Yuanhai; younger brother Sihao; Prince Guiyan of Pingqin; Prince Pu of Wuxing; Lingshan, Governor of Changle; successor son Fuhu
idiomatic: Duke Sheng of Guangping; Duke Yongle of Yangzhou; younger brother Changbi; Prince Xianguo of Xiangle; Prince Sigu of Shangluo; son Yuanhai; younger brother Sihao; Prince Guiyan of Pingqin; Prince Pu of Wuxing; Lingshan, Governor of Changle; successor son Fuhu

literal: Duke Sheng of Guangping was a great-uncle of the Grand Ancestor on the father's side.
idiomatic: Duke Sheng of Guangping was a great-uncle of Gao Huan on the father's side.

literal: Generous and mild, he had the bearing of an elder of worth.
idiomatic: Generous and mild, he had the bearing of an elder of worth.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor raised troops at Xindu, he made Sheng Grand Commander of the Center Army and enfeoffed him Duke of Guangping Commandery.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised troops at Xindu, he made Sheng grand commander of the center army and enfeoffed him duke of Guangping Commandery.

literal: He rose in succession to Minister of Works and Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: He rose in succession to minister of works and grand commandant.

literal: In the third year of Tianping, he died in office.
idiomatic: In the third year of Tianping, he died in office.

literal: Posthumously he was granted the Acting Yellow Battle-Axe, Grand Commandant, Grand Preceptor, and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted the acting yellow battle-axe, grand commandant, grand preceptor, and recorder of affairs of the masters of writing.

literal: Having no son, he made his elder brother's son Ziyuan his heir.
idiomatic: Having no son, he made his elder brother's son Ziyuan his heir.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, his title was changed to Prince of Pingchang; he died while serving as Governor of Wei.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao, his title was changed to prince of Pingchang; he died while serving as governor of Wei.

literal: Duke Yongle of Yangzhou was the son of the Grand Ancestor's father's elder cousin.
idiomatic: Duke Yongle of Yangzhou was the son of Gao Huan's father's elder cousin.

literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he was enfeoffed Baron of Yangzhou County and his rank was advanced to duke.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Taichang, he was enfeoffed baron of Yangzhou County and his rank was advanced to duke.

literal: He rose in succession to Governor of Beiyu Province.
idiomatic: He rose in succession to governor of Beiyu Province.

literal: At the Battle of Heyin, Minister of Works Gao Ang suffered defeat and withdrew.
idiomatic: At the Battle of Heyin, Minister of Works Gao Ang suffered defeat and withdrew.

literal: Yongle held the southern city of Heyang; Ang fled toward the city, and as the Western army's pursuers were about to arrive, Yongle would not open the gate — Ang was thereupon captured by the Western army.
idiomatic: Yongle held the southern city of Heyang; Ang fled toward the city, and as the Western army's pursuers were about to arrive, Yongle would not open the gate — Ang was thereupon captured by the Western army.

literal: The Grand Ancestor was furious and had him beaten two hundred strokes with the staff.
idiomatic: Gao Huan was furious and had him beaten two hundred strokes with the staff.

literal: Later he was removed from Yu Province, and his household estate was not established.
idiomatic: Later he was removed from Yu Province, and his household estate was not established.

literal: The Grand Ancestor asked the reason; he replied, "Pei Jian served as Chief Administrator, and Xin Gongzheng as Vice Director — entrusted by the prince, they would not accept so much as a cup of wine or a chicken.
idiomatic: Gao Huan asked the reason; he replied, "Pei Jian served as chief administrator, and Xin Gongzheng as vice director — entrusted by the prince, they would not accept so much as a cup of wine or a chicken.

literal: " The Grand Ancestor thereupon made Yongle Governor of Ji Province and again appointed Jian and Gongzheng as Chief Administrator and Vice Director.
idiomatic: " Gao Huan thereupon made Yongle governor of Ji Province and again appointed Jian and Gongzheng as chief administrator and vice director.

literal: He said to Yongle, "Do not be too greedy — take a little in propriety and need not fear again.
idiomatic: He said to Yongle, "Do not be too greedy — take a little in propriety and need not fear again.

literal: " When Yongle reached the province, Jian and Gongzheng remonstrated but were not heeded; they submitted a report to the Grand Ancestor.
idiomatic: " When Yongle reached the province, Jian and Gongzheng remonstrated but were not heeded; they submitted a report to Gao Huan.

literal: The Grand Ancestor sealed the report and showed it to Yongle.
idiomatic: Gao Huan sealed the report and showed it to Yongle.

literal: Only then did he know the two men were upright and incorrupt; both were promoted and employed.
idiomatic: Only then did he know the two men were upright and incorrupt; both were promoted and employed.

literal: Yongle died in the province.
idiomatic: Yongle died in the province.

literal: Posthumously he was made Grand Preceptor, Grand Commandant, and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing; his posthumous title was Wuzhao.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was made grand preceptor, grand commandant, and recorder of affairs of the masters of writing; his posthumous title was Wuzhao.

literal: Having no son, his elder cousin Sigu made his second son Xiaoxu his successor to inherit the title.
idiomatic: Having no son, his elder cousin Sigu made his second son Xiaoxu his successor to inherit the title.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, his title was changed to Prince of Xiucheng Commandery.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao, his title was changed to prince of Xiucheng Commandery.

literal: Yongle's younger brother Changbi had the childhood name A'jia.
idiomatic: Yongle's younger brother Changbi had the childhood name A'jia.

literal: By nature coarse and martial, going in and out of the city he liked to beat passersby on the road; people at the time all called him Lord A'jia.
idiomatic: By nature coarse and martial, going in and out of the city he liked to beat passersby on the road; people at the time all called him Lord A'jia.

literal: As a member of the imperial clan he was enfeoffed Prince of Guangwu.
idiomatic: As a member of the imperial clan he was enfeoffed prince of Guangwu.

literal: At that time there was a Daoist monk named Tian'en, extremely violent, who rampaged through the lanes and marketplaces; later he joined Changbi's faction and devoted himself entirely to brawling.
idiomatic: At that time there was a Daoist monk named Tian'en, extremely violent, who rampaged through the lanes and marketplaces; later he joined Changbi's faction and devoted himself entirely to brawling.

literal: Wenxuan arrested and imprisoned them all; more than ten of Tian'en's followers were executed in the marketplace, and Changbi was flogged one hundred strokes.
idiomatic: Gao Yang arrested and imprisoned them all; more than ten of Tian'en's followers were executed in the marketplace, and Changbi was flogged one hundred strokes.

literal: Soon afterward he was made Governor of Southern Ying Province; in the province, for no reason he panicked and fled, rebelled, and entered the Turks — in the end no one knew where he died.
idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made governor of Southern Ying Province; in the province, for no reason he panicked and fled, rebelled, and entered the Turks — in the end no one knew where he died.

literal: Prince Sigu of Shangluo was a nephew of the Grand Ancestor.
idiomatic: Prince Sigu of Shangluo was a nephew of Gao Huan.

literal: By nature generous and mild, he possessed considerable martial ability.
idiomatic: By nature generous and mild, he possessed considerable martial ability.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, he was enfeoffed Prince of Shangluo Commandery.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao, he was enfeoffed prince of Shangluo Commandery.

literal: He rose in succession to Minister of Works and Grand Tutor.
idiomatic: He rose in succession to minister of works and grand tutor.

literal: He died in office.
idiomatic: He died in office.

literal: His son Yuanhai rose in succession to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
idiomatic: His son Yuanhai rose in succession to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

literal: He wished to dwell in mountain forests and cultivate the Buddhist canon.
idiomatic: He wished to dwell in mountain forests and cultivate the Buddhist canon.

literal: Wenxuan granted his request.
idiomatic: Gao Yang granted his request.

literal: He then entered Mount Linlu, and for two years utterly abandoned human affairs; his resolve could not hold firm, and he petitioned asking to return.
idiomatic: He then entered Mount Linlu, and for two years utterly abandoned human affairs; his resolve could not hold firm, and he petitioned asking to return.

literal: Summoned back to his original post, he thereupon gave himself to wine and unrestrained pleasure, widely taking concubines and attendants.
idiomatic: Summoned back to his original post, he thereupon gave himself to wine and unrestrained pleasure, widely taking concubines and attendants.

literal: He was also made Commander of the Army; small in capacity but great in ambition, he rather prided himself on clever stratagems.
idiomatic: He was also made commander of the army; small in capacity but great in ambition, he rather prided himself on clever stratagems.

literal: At the end of the Huangjian era, Xiaozhao visited Jinyang while Wucheng remained on guard; Yuanhai, as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, stayed behind to manage confidential affairs.
idiomatic: At the end of the Huangjian era, Gao Yan visited Jinyang while Gao Zhan remained on guard; Yuanhai, as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, stayed behind to manage confidential affairs.

literal: When Xiaozhao first executed Yang Yin and the others, he had told Wucheng, "When the affair succeeds, I will make you Imperial Younger Brother.
idiomatic: When Gao Yan first executed Yang Yin and the others, he had told Gao Zhan, "When the affair succeeds, I will make you imperial younger brother.

literal: " When he ascended the throne, he made Wucheng hold troops at Ye and established his son Bainian as crown prince — Wucheng was very discontent.
idiomatic: " When he ascended the throne, he made Gao Zhan hold troops at Ye and established his son Bainian as crown prince — Gao Zhan was very discontent.

literal: Before this, the Prince of Ji'nan had always been kept at Ye; Kudi Fulian was made Governor of You Province, and Hulu Fengle was made Commander of the Army — both to divide Wucheng's power.
idiomatic: Before this, the Prince of Ji'nan had always been kept at Ye; Kudi Fulian was made governor of You Province, and Hulu Fengle was made commander of the army — both to divide Gao Zhan's power.

literal: Wucheng kept Fulian but would not allow Fengle to assume his duties.
idiomatic: Gao Zhan kept Fulian but would not allow Fengle to assume his duties.

literal: He then joined Prince Xiaoyu of Henan in a feigned hunt, plotting in the wild, and returned only after dark.
idiomatic: He then joined Prince Xiaoyu of Henan in a feigned hunt, plotting in the wild, and returned only after dark.

literal: Before this a children's rhyme said, "At Zhongxing Temple, a white duck old man — from the four quarters they listen, the sound harmonious; the Daoist hears it and at night strikes the bell.
idiomatic: Before this a children's rhyme said, "At Zhongxing Temple, a white duck old man — from the four quarters they listen, the sound harmonious; the Daoist hears it and at night strikes the bell.

literal: " At that time the chancellor's headquarters was in the northern city — that is, the old Zhongxing Temple.
idiomatic: " At that time the chancellor's headquarters was in the northern city — that is, the old Zhongxing Temple.

literal: "Duck old man" means rooster — it pointed to Wucheng's childhood name Buluoqi.
idiomatic: "Duck old man" means rooster — it pointed to Gao Zhan's childhood name Buluoqi.

literal: "The Daoist" was the Prince of Ji'nan's childhood name.
idiomatic: "The Daoist" was the Prince of Ji'nan's childhood name.

literal: "Strikes the bell" meant he would be beaten.
idiomatic: "Strikes the bell" meant he would be beaten.

literal: Soon afterward the court astrologer memorialized that there was an emperor's aura in the northern city.
idiomatic: Soon afterward the court astrologer memorialized that there was an emperor's aura in the northern city.

literal: Emperor Zhao thought the Prince of Ji'nan corresponded to it; he therefore sent Prince Guiyan of Pingqin to Ye to welcome the Prince of Ji'nan to Bing Province.
idiomatic: Gao Yan thought the Prince of Ji'nan corresponded to it; he therefore sent Prince Guiyan of Pingqin to Ye to welcome the Prince of Ji'nan to Bing Province.

literal: Wucheng first consulted Yuanhai and also asked for a plan to secure himself.
idiomatic: Gao Zhan first consulted Yuanhai and also asked for a plan to secure himself.

literal: Yuanhai said, "The Empress Dowager enjoys boundless fortune; the emperor's filial nature is extraordinary — Your Highness need not worry otherwise.
idiomatic: Yuanhai said, "The Empress Dowager enjoys boundless fortune; the emperor's filial nature is extraordinary — Your Highness need not worry otherwise.

literal: " Wucheng said, "Is this truly the meaning of my open-hearted sincerity?
idiomatic: " Gao Zhan said, "Is this truly the meaning of my open-hearted sincerity?

literal: " Yuanhai asked to return to his quarters and think on it one night.
idiomatic: " Yuanhai asked to return to his quarters and think on it one night.

literal: Wucheng kept Yuanhai in the rear hall.
idiomatic: Gao Zhan kept Yuanhai in the rear hall.

literal: Yuanhai went all night without sleep, only pacing slowly around the bed.
idiomatic: Yuanhai went all night without sleep, only pacing slowly around the bed.

literal: Before dawn Wucheng hurried out and said, "What is your divine calculation?
idiomatic: Before dawn Gao Zhan hurried out and said, "What is your divine calculation?

literal: " He answered, "In the night I obtained three stratagems — I fear they may not be usable.
idiomatic: " He answered, "In the night I obtained three stratagems — I fear they may not be usable.

literal: " He then spoke of Prince Xiao of Liang, who fearing execution entered the passes, and proposed that with a few horsemen he enter Jinyang, first see the Empress Dowager and beg mercy, then see the sovereign and request removal of military authority, taking death as his limit and seeking not to interfere in court governance — he would surely preserve the security of Mount Tai.
idiomatic: " He then spoke of Prince Xiao of Liang, who fearing execution entered the passes, and proposed that with a few horsemen he enter Jinyang, first see the Empress Dowager and beg mercy, then see the sovereign and request removal of military authority, taking death as his limit and seeking not to interfere in court governance — he would surely preserve the security of Mount Tai.

literal: This was the upper stratagem.
idiomatic: This was the upper stratagem.

literal: If not, he should submit a memorial stating, "'My authority and power are too great; I fear I will draw slander from the multitude' — and request the governorships of Qing and Qi Provinces.
idiomatic: If not, he should submit a memorial stating, "'My authority and power are too great; I fear I will draw slander from the multitude' — and request the governorships of Qing and Qi Provinces.

literal: Dwelling in quiet and keeping to himself, he would surely not invite public criticism.
idiomatic: Dwelling in quiet and keeping to himself, he would surely not invite public criticism.

literal: This was the middle stratagem.
idiomatic: This was the middle stratagem.

literal: " When asked further about the lower stratagem he said, "To speak would mean immediate execution of the whole clan.
idiomatic: " When asked further about the lower stratagem he said, "To speak would mean immediate execution of the whole clan.

literal: " Pressed, he answered, "The Prince of Ji'nan is the legitimate heir; the sovereign seized the throne through the Empress Dowager's order.
idiomatic: " Pressed, he answered, "The Prince of Ji'nan is the legitimate heir; the sovereign seized the throne through the Empress Dowager's order.

literal: Now gather the civil and military officials, display this edict, seize Fengle, behead Guiyan, honor the Prince of Ji'nan, and proclaim to the realm — with righteousness to punish rebellion, this would be a once-in-ten-thousand-generations opportunity.
idiomatic: Now gather the civil and military officials, display this edict, seize Fengle, behead Guiyan, honor the Prince of Ji'nan, and proclaim to the realm — with righteousness to punish rebellion, this would be a once-in-ten-thousand-generations opportunity.

literal: " Wucheng was greatly pleased but hesitated, and in the end could not adopt it.
idiomatic: " Gao Zhan was greatly pleased but hesitated, and in the end could not adopt it.

literal: He then had Zheng Daoqian perform divination; all said, "It is unfavorable to act; quiet brings good fortune.
idiomatic: He then had Zheng Daoqian perform divination; all said, "It is unfavorable to act; quiet brings good fortune.

literal: " He also summoned Cao Weizu and questioned him on state affairs.
idiomatic: " He also summoned Cao Weizu and questioned him on state affairs.

literal: He replied, "There will be great misfortune.
idiomatic: He replied, "There will be great misfortune.

literal: " At that time the Magistrate of Linlu, surnamed Pan, knew divination and omens; he secretly told Wucheng, "The imperial carriage will break at dusk — Your Highness will be sovereign of the realm.
idiomatic: " At that time the Magistrate of Linlu, surnamed Pan, knew divination and omens; he secretly told Gao Zhan, "The imperial carriage will break at dusk — Your Highness will be sovereign of the realm.

literal: " Wucheng detained him inside to wait for the outcome.
idiomatic: " Gao Zhan detained him inside to wait for the outcome.

literal: He also had shamans perform divination; most said there was no need to raise troops — great good fortune would come of itself.
idiomatic: He also had shamans perform divination; most said there was no need to raise troops — great good fortune would come of itself.

literal: Wucheng thereupon obeyed the edict and sent several hundred horsemen to escort the Prince of Ji'nan to Jinyang.
idiomatic: Gao Zhan thereupon obeyed the edict and sent several hundred horsemen to escort the Prince of Ji'nan to Jinyang.

literal: When Xiaozhao died and Wucheng ascended the throne, Yuanhai was made Palace Attendant, Opener of a Government Office Equal in Protocol to Three Imperators, and Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.
idiomatic: When Gao Yan died and Gao Zhan ascended the throne, Yuanhai was made palace attendant, opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators, and grand tutor to the crown prince.

literal: In the second year of Heqing, Yuanhai was slandered by He Shikai and was beaten sixty strokes with the horsewhip.
idiomatic: In the second year of Heqing, Yuanhai was slandered by He Shikai and was beaten sixty strokes with the horsewhip.

literal: He was rebuked, "You at Ye told me to rebel as younger brother against elder brother — how many acts of unrighteousness were there!
idiomatic: He was rebuked, "You at Ye told me to rebel as younger brother against elder brother — how many acts of unrighteousness were there!

literal: Ye's troops and horses resisting Bing Province — how many acts of folly were there!
idiomatic: Ye's troops and horses resisting Bing Province — how many acts of folly were there!

literal: Unrighteous and foolish — how could you be employed?
idiomatic: Unrighteous and foolish — how could you be employed?

literal: " He was sent out as Governor of Yan Province.
idiomatic: " He was sent out as governor of Yan Province.

literal: Yuanhai's later wife was a niece of Empress Dowager Lu; for this reason he was soon recalled and given employment again.
idiomatic: Yuanhai's later wife was a niece of Empress Dowager Lu; for this reason he was soon recalled and given employment again.

literal: In the Wuping era he jointly held court governance with Zu Ting.
idiomatic: In the Wuping era he jointly held court governance with Zu Ting.

literal: Yuanhai often reported the Empress Dowager's confidential words to Ting.
idiomatic: Yuanhai often reported the Empress Dowager's confidential words to Ting.

literal: Ting sought the post of Commander of the Army; Yuanhai would not agree — Ting thereupon reported what Yuanhai had told him to the Empress Dowager.
idiomatic: Ting sought the post of commander of the army; Yuanhai would not agree — Ting thereupon reported what Yuanhai had told him to the Empress Dowager.

literal: The Empress Dowager was angry and sent Yuanhai out as Governor of Zheng Province.
idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was angry and sent Yuanhai out as governor of Zheng Province.

literal: When Ye was about to fall, he was summoned and made Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: When Ye was about to fall, he was summoned and made director of the masters of writing.

literal: In the seventh year of Jiande of Zhou, at Ye he plotted rebellion and was executed.
idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jiande of Zhou, at Ye he plotted rebellion and was executed.

literal: Yuanhai loved disorder and delighted in calamity, yet feigned benevolence — he did not drink wine or eat meat.
idiomatic: Yuanhai loved disorder and delighted in calamity, yet feigned benevolence — he did not drink wine or eat meat.

literal: In the last years of Tianbao, Wenxuan revered and believed in the inner Buddhist law, even to the point that the ancestral temple had no blood offerings — all was Yuanhai's counsel.
idiomatic: In the last years of Tianbao, Gao Yang revered and believed in the inner Buddhist law, even to the point that the ancestral temple had no blood offerings — all was Yuanhai's counsel.

literal: When he was Right Vice Minister, he again persuaded the Last Emperor to forbid slaughter and cut off the sale of wine.
idiomatic: When he was right vice minister, he again persuaded the Last Emperor to forbid slaughter and cut off the sale of wine.

literal: Yet his heart was not truly at peace — therefore in the end he brought on ruin.
idiomatic: Yet his heart was not truly at peace — therefore in the end he brought on ruin.

literal: Sigu's younger brother Sihao.
idiomatic: Sigu's younger brother Sihao.

literal: Sihao was originally a son of the Hao clan; Sigu raised him as a younger brother but treated him very poorly.
idiomatic: Sihao was originally a son of the Hao clan; Sigu raised him as a younger brother but treated him very poorly.

literal: In youth he served the Imperial Founder in horsemanship and archery.
idiomatic: In youth he served Gao Cheng in horsemanship and archery.
